findings.text: Provides 128-bit logical right shift with zero fill, leaving value unchanged for zero shift, merging low and high halves for shifts below word width, and moving high half into low position with zeroed high half for larger shifts.
Exposes a copy operation that duplicates a byte range from source to destination and then makes the destination range clean to point of persistence, requiring cacheable destination.

Offers position independent data cache maintenance over an address interval to point of coherency, with separate entry points for clean plus invalidate, invalidate with and without final ordering barrier, and clean with and without final ordering barrier.

Offers clean to point of persistence when hardware persist support is present, otherwise transparently redirects to clean to point of coherency, preserving the same interval contract and final ordering.

Defines a fault dispatch record pairing a handler function over fault address, syndrome and register state with a signal number, signal code and descriptive name, with a forward declared table indexed by syndrome.
Initial generation value for address space identifier allocation equals one shifted left by sixteen.

Count of usable user address space identifiers is two raised to the configured bit width, halved when the kernel is unmapped at exception level zero, with identifier zero reserved and at least one spare slot preserved beyond per-CPU reservations and pins.

Pin and unpin paths serialize against allocation and rollover under a single global address space identifier spinlock held with interrupts saved, covering generation checks, bitmap updates and pin counts.
Exposes paired operations to pin an address space identifier for a memory descriptor with reference counted sharing and to release it, returning zero when pinning is unavailable or exhausted.

Allocator starts with empty maps and first generation, pre-reserving kernel identifiers when needed, and enforces that usable count exceeds processor count with reserved headroom, capping pins to leave one free slot after rollover.
Exposes page copy helpers that duplicate content between high memory pages, with the user variant additionally ensuring data cache coherence for the destination.

On memory tagging capable systems, tag state follows content with distinct handling for huge versus single pages, propagating across subpages only for tagged huge sources starting at first subpage and otherwise copying tags to a newly taggable destination while resetting hardware address tags when enabled.
Flushing a page is defined as flushing its enclosing folio, which is a no-op except for clearing a cached clean marker when present.

Exposes direction-aware direct memory access synchronization that cleans to coherency point for device-bound transfers without final barrier, invalidates without barrier for processor-bound transfers except device-to-device direction which is a no-op, plus a coherent preparation that cleans with ordering.

Device direct memory access setup treats devices as coherent when no cache levels are reported, warns and taints when non-coherent alignment exceeds architectural minimum, records coherence attribute, and delegates to hypervisor setup.

User access fault attribution matches fault direction against encoded access direction, and instruction classification reports true for any table entry except unlisted addresses and mismatched copy entries.

Exception fixup resolves the faulting instruction address in the table, then dispatches by entry type to error-zero with register poisoning, direction-checked copy resume, unaligned load zero padding with endian-aware shifting, or packet filter handling, failing when unlisted and faulting otherwise.

Kernel abort predicates distinguish current-level instruction and data aborts by exception class, recognize permission faults directly or via translation fault under privileged protect with access flag, and identify hypervisor-injected stage-two aborts by initialization plus page-table-walk indicator.

Spurious kernel translation assessment re-walks the address with interrupts masked and treats the fault as ignorable when translation now succeeds or when re-walk reports a different fault class, with a reclaim path for hypervisor protected pages.
Tag fault reporting is either active, deriving write direction from syndrome and reporting through sanitizer with fault address and program counter, or compiled to no-op.

Kernel fault handling prefers table fixup for non-instruction faults, then suppresses spurious translations with rate limited warning, then recovers tag check faults by reporting and disabling tag checking locally with barrier, then classifies permission, null, hypervisor and paging cases with special allocator and runtime fixup chances before dying.

User bad areas record sanitized syndrome where kernel addresses are presented as level zero translation faults preserving only low-risk bits and faulting safely on unexpected classes, then signal via table entry; kernel bad areas delegate to kernel fault path after untagging.

Page fault permission requirements derive from abort kind: execution demands execute, guarded control stack faults demand write even for reads to trigger copy-on-write, write aborts demand write, reads demand read with write and conditionally execute when enhanced privilege protection is absent.
Copy with cache clean assumes cacheable destination and provides no explicit barrier between copy and maintenance, so non-cacheable use risks ordering loss.
Halving of identifier space under unmapped-at-privilege kernels plus per-processor reservations and pins risks exhaustion after rollover if headroom checks are ignored.
Provides a kernel fixup entry that attempts synchronous exception recovery and reports success.
Unaligned load fixup reads the containing aligned word and shifts by fault offset with endian-specific direction, so concurrency or device memory aliasing risks torn or side-effecting reads.
